plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch adjustment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples, human kidney) with a balanced 2-batch, 6-vs-6 treated/control design. The knowledge-grounded DESeq2 workflow is used throughout: sample-structure QC to confirm the batch does not dominate variance and no sample is an outlier; a minimal pre-filter; median-of-ratios normalization inside the model; a two-factor design (~ batch + condition) so batch is adjusted as a covariate rather than removed from the counts; the Wald test with apeglm shrinkage for effect sizes; BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05 to call DE genes; and preranked fgsea on the Wald statistic against Hallmark then Reactome pathways (both staged locally) to interpret the full ranked gene list, since ORA is disallowed here and would in any case be underpowered if <50 genes reach significance. An edgeR quasi-likelihood run on the same design gives a second-method robustness check on the DE calls, as recommended for 6 replicates per group. A final report step consolidates diagnostics, gene tables, enrichment tables, and a full reproducibility record.
